title: What Is 420?
seoTitle: What Is 420? The Story Behind April 20 | Uforia Dispensary
description: Why does 420 mean cannabis? Here is the origin story most often told, from a group of 1971 San Rafael students, and how April 20 became a cannabis holiday.
lede: You have probably seen 420 on T-shirts, posters and calendars. The number has become shorthand for cannabis culture, and April 20 is now an informal holiday. Here is how it is commonly said to have started.

sections.heading: The story most people tell
sections.html:
The most widely cited account begins in 1971 at San Rafael High School in Marin County, California. A group of friends, later nicknamed the Waldos because they liked to hang out by a wall outside the school, are said to have agreed to meet at 4:20 in the afternoon, after classes and sports practice were over.

As the story goes, they had heard about an abandoned patch of cannabis plants growing somewhere near the Point Reyes Peninsula, along with a rough map showing where to find it. They would meet by a statue of Louis Pasteur on campus at 4:20 and set off to search. They never found the plants, but 420 stuck as their private code word for cannabis, a handy way to talk about it in front of parents and teachers.

sections.heading: From a school wall to the whole world
sections.html:
The phrase might have stayed a local in-joke if not for the Grateful Dead. According to the usual telling, members of the group had connections to people around the band, and the code spread through the Dead's large, traveling community of fans.

In 1990, Grateful Dead fans in Oakland handed out a flyer inviting people to gather on April 20 at 4:20 p.m. A copy reached High Times magazine, which printed it the following year, and from there the idea traveled far beyond California. Over the decades that followed, 4/20 grew from a counterculture wink into a date nearly everyone recognizes.

sections.heading: Myths that never quite fit
sections.html: Plenty of other explanations have circulated over the years. Some claim 420 was a police radio code for cannabis, others that it is the number of chemical compounds in the plant. Neither holds up well. The San Rafael story remains the most commonly accepted origin, even if, like many good legends, a few of its details are hard to confirm.

sections.heading: How people celebrate April 20 today
sections.html:
Today, April 20 is an unofficial holiday for cannabis enthusiasts. People mark it with gatherings among friends, music, cannabis-friendly events and a quiet nod to the clock at 4:20 p.m. For many dispensaries, it is one of the busiest days of the year.

If you are celebrating, the same good habits apply as on any other day. Start low and go slow, stay hydrated, and plan a sober ride if you will be heading anywhere. Our safe consumption page has more practical tips, and for New Jersey's rules, see is weed legal in New Jersey?

takeaways: The most commonly told origin traces 420 to a group of San Rafael, California, students in 1971.
It began as a code for meeting up at 4:20 in the afternoon.
Grateful Dead fans and High Times magazine helped spread it worldwide.
April 20 is now an informal holiday for cannabis culture.
